status: registered before any reconstruction run; amendments must be logged in amendments.md
provenance: This implementation is an independent reconstruction of the experimental procedures described in Woodyard (2026), using the documented mathematical definitions, simulation parameters, random seeds, and repository snapshot. The original execution scripts and machine-readable results were unavailable. Implementation choices not specified in the manuscript are explicitly documented as reconstruction assumptions. All reported replication results are generated by the reconstructed implementation and are not represented as recovered original outputs.
goal: Test whether the scientific findings of the v3 sections (rooting under memory, resonance testing, QBO exploratory checks) hold under an independent implementation, and compare every reported Monte Carlo value with its reconstructed counterpart. Exact numerical agreement is not expected because the original random-number streams cannot be recovered.
no_tuning_rule: Implementation choices are fixed in this file before any study run. No choice may be changed after study results are seen in order to move a number toward the paper. Bug fixes found after a run are allowed only if logged in amendments.md with the reason, and the pre-fix result is kept.

procedures.v2: drr_framework.modules.RootingAnalyzer.analyze on raw series (unchanged since commit 862c4f7), circular shift, heuristic candidate gate as implemented, random_state = row_seed + 1 + trial
procedures.v3: The same RootingAnalyzer call on per-channel AR(p) innovations, same random_state
procedures.granger: Pairwise F-test for every ordered pair; Bonferroni over ordered pairs at alpha

size.seeds: AR(1) rows use the committed calibration-study seeds (seed + 10000*(i+1) for coefficient index i in [0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.97]), so the v2 column must reproduce results/expected/rooting_calibration_study.json exactly; the AR(2) row uses seed + 50000

memory.seeds: seed + 300000 + 1000*k for row index k; the first 200 trials of the first four v2 rows must reproduce the committed memory rows exactly

metrics.exact: the true edge dim_0 -> dim_1 significant at the true lag
metrics.any_lag: the true edge significant at any lag (Granger: pair 0->1 rejected)

resonance_study.seeds: family index j: seed + 1000*j (nulls first, then alternatives, in the order listed)

procedures.dstar_ar1: Monte Carlo p of depth against 99 Gaussian AR(1) series with the sample lag-1 autocorrelation; reject if p <= alpha
procedures.dstar_isotonic: Monte Carlo p of depth against 99 Gaussian series synthesized from the linear-scale isotonic periodogram fit; reject if p <= alpha
procedures.lambda: Spectral-excess statistic, Eq. (4), against 99 refitted Gaussian surrogates with spectrum S-hat; reject if p <= alpha; record argmax bin

qbo_checks.data: vendored NOAA CPC 30 and 50 hPa indices via drr_framework.external_benchmark.qbo.load_qbo_series (572 months)
quantities: v2 and v3 best lag and adjusted p for 30->50 and 50->30, and whether each passes the candidate gate
share of interior periodogram power in bins 18-24
D* p-values under the AR(1) and isotonic nulls
Lambda p-value, argmax period in months and its ratio, and the QBO-band ratio

assumptions.choice: drr_framework.calibration.simulate_ar1: unit-variance innovations, stationary first value, 200-sample burn-in; coupled design from simulate_directed_pair (unit-variance channels, target = c*source(t-d) + sqrt(1-c^2)*u)
assumptions.reason: The paper states its v2 rows share seeds with the committed calibration study, which uses these generators

assumptions.choice: x_t = 2 r cos(2 pi f0) x_{t-1} - r^2 x_{t-2} + e_t, f0 = 0.0625, standard normal e_t, zero start, 200-sample burn-in, scaled to unit theoretical variance; coupled design uses the same construction as A1 with AR(2) channels
assumptions.reason: Frequency not stated for the rooting oscillator; 0.0625 is the paper's line frequency

assumptions.choice: a*sin(2 pi 0.0625 t + U(0, 2 pi)) added to a unit-variance background; SNR = 10 log10(a^2/2), so a = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 give -15.1, -9.0, -5.5, -3.0 dB; AR(0.9) backgrounds are scaled to unit theoretical variance
assumptions.reason: Matches the committed depth reference (amplitudes 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 at the same dB labels)

assumptions.choice: Per channel, OLS AR(p) with intercept for p = 0..p_max (10 in simulation, 12 for QBO), all candidate fits on the common sample t = p_max+1..T; p chosen by AIC = n log(RSS/n) + 2(p+1); innovations of the chosen fit on t = p_max+1..T, so every channel is trimmed to T - p_max aligned samples
assumptions.reason: Not stated beyond AIC and p <= 10

assumptions.choice: For target j and source i: own-lag order q chosen by AIC (same rule as A5, q = 1..10) on the target alone; unrestricted OLS adds source lags 1..4; F-test of the four source coefficients; common sample t = 11..T; Bonferroni alpha/6 over the six ordered pairs; reported lag = source lag with largest |coefficient| (not scored)
assumptions.reason: Not stated beyond AIC own lags, source lags 1-4 and Bonferroni

assumptions.choice: I_k = |FFT(x - mean)_k|^2 / T at interior bins k = 1..floor(T/2)-1
assumptions.reason: Paper defines interior bins; scaling is irrelevant to Lambda and to the null fits

assumptions.choice: L2 pool-adjacent-violators fits, non-increasing and non-decreasing; the direction with the smaller residual sum of squares is used; ties go to non-increasing. Lambda fits log I_k; the D* isotonic null fits I_k on the linear scale

Complex Fourier coefficients X_k = sqrt(T S_k / 2) (N1 + i N2) at interior bins, zero at k = 0 and at Nyquist, inverse real FFT to length T; each Lambda surrogate is refitted with its own isotonic log fit
phi-hat = sample lag-1 autocorrelation of the demeaned series, clipped to [-0.99, 0.99]; null series from simulate_ar1
assumptions.reason: Paper: AR(1) matched to the sample lag-1 autocorrelation

assumptions.choice: p = (1 + #{null >= observed}) / (B + 1) for depth and Lambda

assumptions.reason: Not stated for the QBO checks; matches the simulation depth window

assumptions.choice: numpy.random.default_rng (PCG64) with the integer seeds listed here; original seed spawning unknown
Whatever Python/NumPy/SciPy the run uses is recorded in each artifact; it differs from the original

comparison_rules.monte_carlo_rates: For every rate the paper reports with a stated trial count n, the paper count is round(rate*n). Each reconstructed count is compared with it by a two-sided Fisher exact test. Holm correction is applied across all compared rates. A cell is 'consistent' if its Holm-adjusted p is at least 0.05 and 'differs' otherwise. Raw p, the difference and both rates are reported for every cell.
comparison_rules.exact_reproductions: The four committed v2 size rows and the first 200 trials of four committed memory rows must match exactly; any mismatch is reported as a reconstruction defect.
comparison_rules.qbo: Lag-1 autocorrelations: consistent if equal after rounding to two decimals. Variance share in bins 18-24: consistent if between 0.4 and 0.6 ('about half'). Monte Carlo p-values: consistent if on the same side of 0.05. Edge lags and argmax periods: consistent if equal (periods within 0.5 months).

findings.claim: v2 exact-lag recovery falls with memory; v3 recovers the edge at the true lag regardless of memory
findings.rule: v2 exact rate at phi=0.97 below its rate at phi=0.5 and below 0.6 at phi=0.9; v3 exact rate at least 0.95 in every memory row

findings.claim: Memory makes v2 report the target leading its source; prewhitening removes it
findings.rule: v2 reverse-edge Wilson lower bound above 0.05 at phi=0.9; v3 reverse rate at most 0.02 in every AR(1) memory row

findings.claim: All three rooting procedures hold size on the five nulls
findings.rule: every size row's Wilson lower bound at most 0.05 for v2, v3 and Granger

findings.claim: v3 and Granger have similar power at phi=0.9
findings.rule: absolute difference in any-lag power at most 0.05 at c=0.1 and c=0.2

findings.claim: On coupled oscillators v2 localizes the lag poorly and v3 does not
findings.rule: v2 exact rate below 0.5 and v3 exact rate at least 0.95 for the AR(2) memory row

findings.claim: A fixed depth cutoff is a red-noise detector
findings.rule: fixed-cut false-alarm rate at least 0.9 on AR(0.9) and AR(0.97)

findings.claim: The AR(1)-calibrated D* fails under misspecification; isotonic D* and Lambda hold size
findings.rule: AR(1)-D* Wilson lower bound above 0.05 on AR(0.9)+white; isotonic D* and Lambda Wilson lower bounds at most 0.05 on all five nulls

findings.claim: Only Lambda detects lines in red backgrounds
findings.rule: Lambda rate at least 0.5 and both D* rates at most 0.1 for the -9.0 dB line in AR(0.9)
argmax within one bin of k = 32 in at least 90% of Lambda rejections for the -9.0 dB line in AR(0.9)

findings.claim: Broad oscillators are not identifiable from a monotone continuum at T = 512
findings.rule: Lambda rate below 0.15 for r = 0.8 and r = 0.9

findings.claim: On the QBO, Lambda rejects the monotone null at both levels while D* does not reject
findings.rule: Lambda p <= 0.05 at both levels; all four D* p-values > 0.05

findings.claim: On the QBO both rooting operators report 30 -> 50 hPa
findings.rule: 30->50 adjusted p <= 0.05 for v2 and v3
